## Problem 1.2: Cooling an air stream {.unnumbered}

A stream of 200 kg/h of air is cooled from 150 $^\circ$C to 40 $^\circ$C at constant
pressure with no phase change.

Determine the cooling requirement in kW.

$C_P = 1.005\ \text{kJ}\,\text{kg}^{-1}\,\text{K}^{-1}$

::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions"}

::: {.callout-note icon=false collapse="true" title="Solution"}

The general energy balance is:
$$\frac{d(m_{sys}H_{sys})}{dt} = \sum \dot{m}_{in}H_{in} - \sum \dot{m}_{out}H_{out} + \dot{Q} + \dot{W}$$
Assume steady-state, no work and a single mass flow in and out:
$$0 = \dot{m}_{in}H_{in} - \dot{m}_{out}H_{out} + \dot{Q} + 0$$
$$-\dot{Q} = \dot{m}(H_{in}-H_{out})$$

Sensible heat only:
$$
\begin{aligned}
(H_{in}-H_{out}) & = \int^{in}_{out} C_P dT \\
                & = C_P \int^{in}_{out} dT \\
                & = C_P (T_{in}-T_{out})
\end{aligned}
$$
add this to the energy balance (note the sign on $\dot{Q}$):
$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot{Q} & = \dot{m} C_P (T_{out}-T_{in}) \\
& = (200)(1.005)(40 - 150) \\
& = -22{,}110\ \text{kJ/h}\\
& = - 6.14\ \text{kW}
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

:::
